claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
claims.evidence: Every legal no-teleport transition has two distinct endpoints sharing at least one live feature and therefore deletes at least two live occurrences. A play has at most floor(L/2) transitions. A certificate comprising its starting tile and destination sequence has polynomial length, and exact simulation verifies legality, simultaneous deletion of all live common features, and final exhaustion in polynomial time.
claims.witness: Certificate form: a tile sequence (t_0,...,t_k) with k at most floor(L/2).
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the decreasing-occurrence invariant from the source rules and checked it in the exact simulator on all enumerated instances and constructed plays.

claims.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
claims.evidence: In any solution, the transitions deleting a feature pair its support into a perfect matching. An unordered tile pair cannot recur, and every transition deletes a feature, so the play is an Euler trail of the simple union. A nonmatching edge between two support vertices must occur after the matching deletion at one endpoint, giving the stated precedence condition. Conversely, suppose the earliest designated matching event to fail is m_f(u), because an earlier nonmatching edge uw deleted f at u. Since m_f(u) is later, precedence forces m_f(w) before uw. That earlier matching event succeeded by minimality, so f was already absent at w when uw occurred, a contradiction. Thus every matching event succeeds; every union edge is legal and all occurrences are deleted.
claims.witness: For necessity, M_f is formed by the actual transitions deleting f. For sufficiency, the ordered Euler trail itself is the solution certificate.
claims.search_method: Proved both implications with a first-failed-matching-event argument; independently compared the characterization with exact reachability on 192 four-tile instances, including overlapping four-support features.

claims.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
claims.evidence: A feature supported on {u,v} can only be deleted by transition uv. All features with that same support are simultaneously deleted on its first traversal, so they represent one simple edge. Consequently a solution is exactly an Euler trail through the graph containing one edge for each distinct support pair. Connectivity of edge-bearing vertices and zero or two odd degrees is necessary and sufficient. Endpoint collection, radix sorting and deduplication of compact integer pairs, followed by connectivity and parity tests, is linear in the explicit input size on the stated word-RAM model; duplicate features do not affect the bound.
claims.witness: The compressed graph K has one edge uv for every distinct two-tile feature support {u,v}; any Euler trail of K is the corresponding no-teleport play.
claims.search_method: Direct equivalence proof plus exhaustive comparison of exact reachability with the Euler criterion on 91 small instances, including duplicate supports.

claims.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
claims.evidence: The draft's five-tile instance is exactly unreachable after 95 memoized states while its displayed matching union admits an open Euler trail. The claim also survives the strict all-even meaning of 'Eulerian': take four tiles and two distinct features, each supported on all four tiles. Choose matchings {01,23} and {02,13}; their simple union is the connected 4-cycle 0-1-3-2-0. Nevertheless, the first move deletes both features at its two endpoints, leaves the current tile featureless, and strands the two remaining live tiles. Thus the instance is unsolvable without teleporting.
claims.witness: Tiles 0,1,2,3 with features a and b both supported on {0,1,2,3}; choose M_a={01,23} and M_b={02,13}. The union is a 4-cycle but no no-teleport solution exists.
claims.search_method: Exact state-space exhaustion of both the draft's five-tile witness and the independent strict 4-cycle witness, followed by direct verification of the displayed perfect matchings and degrees.

claims.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
claims.evidence: The state (current tile, live-occurrence mask) completely determines all future moves, giving at most n*2^L states. For each state, testing all n-1 destinations and scanning at most L incidences costs O(nL). Every transition strictly reduces the mask's population, so the recurrence is acyclic and exact. Memoization shared across all starting tiles therefore costs O(n^2 L*2^L) time and O(n*2^L) table space.
claims.witness: The recurrence accepts mask zero and otherwise branches from (v,M) to every (w,M') obtained by the source's simultaneous-deletion rule.
claims.search_method: Derived the state bound and monotonicity directly; compared memoized reachability with independent path enumeration on 192 small instances and asserted the state and transition-count bounds.

claims.claim: For every simple cubic graph G, one can construct in linear time a sharing-number-4 Tiles instance I(G) that is solvable without teleport moves if and only if G has a Hamiltonian cycle.
claims.evidence: The forward ordering is legal: traverse a Hamiltonian cycle on layer 0, pass through the starting relay to layer 1, traverse the layer-1 cycle while splicing each nonstarting local triangle, and finish on the starting rung. Layer-0 deletions prevent selected features from being prematurely deleted by later rungs; unselected features are deleted at their two endpoint rungs. Conversely, every four-occurrence edge feature induces either the local-local matching or one of the two cross-cross matchings. Calling the latter selected, the forced local triangles and simplicity of G give deg_H(x^0)=deg_H(x^1)=2+s_x and deg_H(r_x)=2 without edge-collapse. If k vertices have odd s_x, H has 2k odd vertices. Euler-trail parity gives k at most one, while the handshaking lemma makes k even, hence k=0. Connectivity of the solution trail contracts to connectivity of the selected spanning subgraph. Thus every s_x is positive and even; cubicity forces s_x=2, so the selected edges form one spanning cycle.
claims.witness: For a Hamiltonian cycle C, the explicit forward certificate has 5|V| transitions: layer-0 C, two starting side edges, layer-1 C with each nonstarting triangle spliced in, then the starting rung.
claims.search_method: Universal forward-and-reverse proof; exact checks over every labeled simple cubic graph on 4 and 6 vertices, 20,412 explicit matching choices for K4 and K3,3, and all 32,768 selected-edge subsets of the Petersen graph.

claims.claim: Deciding no-teleport solvability is NP-hard even when the sharing number is at most 4, every feature occurs on two or four tiles, and every tile contains at most five features.
claims.evidence: Claim 5 supplies a linear many-one reduction from the standard NP-complete Hamiltonian Cycle problem on simple cubic graphs. The construction has 3|V| tiles and 3|V|+|E| features. Private features have frequency two and edge features frequency four. Relay tiles contain two features; each layer tile contains two private features and three incident edge features, totaling five. The pair x^0,x^1 shares its private rung plus the three incident edge features, totaling four; simplicity of G makes every other pair share at most one.
claims.witness: Construction parameters are 3|V| tiles, 3|V|+|E| features, and 6|V|+4|E| occurrences, with maximum feature frequency 4, tile size 5, and sharing number 4.
claims.search_method: Reduction audit and symbolic incidence counting, corroborated exactly on all enumerated cubic fixtures and the Petersen graph.

claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem is NP-complete, and remains NP-complete under the restrictions in the preceding claim.
claims.evidence: Claim 0 establishes NP membership for every explicitly represented instance. Claim 6 establishes NP-hardness for the stated restricted subclass, and therefore also for the unrestricted problem. The same polynomial verifier applies to the subclass, so both decision problems are NP-complete.
claims.witness: The reduction family I(G) supplies hardness certificates, while a polynomial-length tile sequence supplies NP certificates for positive instances.
claims.search_method: Combined the independently verified membership invariant with the independently verified restricted reduction and checked that the promise restrictions are preserved.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a full complexity classification of arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport Tiles via either a polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result. The verified cubic-Hamiltonian-cycle reduction proves NP-hardness even for sharing number 4, and the verified occurrence-decrease argument proves membership in NP. Therefore the draft establishes NP-completeness at the requested strength, rather than merely an auxiliary or restricted result. Its claimed_resolution of FULL and its final NP-completeness headline are accurate—neither overstated nor understated.
